source.title: Structured Features Overfit Where Random Features Grok
source.authors: Chon-Fai Kam; M. Bessafi; Frédéric Cadet

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations have minor formatting artifacts, but the text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests a structured-feature modular-arithmetic setting and reports that the delayed generalization effect does not appear there, refining the scope of grokking claims.
record.gate_note: The paper's own band-sweep and masking results, plus its M = 24 training trajectory, bear on V1. The cited results from other papers are not recorded. The static representability checks and the closed-form results at λ = 10⁻⁶ do not test delayed generalization.
record.test_reason: On modular subtraction (p = 97, 40% train split), the study trains a linear ridge read-out over a fixed band-limited Fourier feature map at λ = 10⁻². It reports no memorize-then-generalize delay. Small active bands give high held-out accuracy, which the authors call gapless; larger bands collapse. This bears on V1, the delayed jump on algorithmic data, in a new kind of system. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with additions. On a band-limited character feature map with a linear ridge read-out at positive weight decay (λ = 10⁻²), a representable target is learned at once when the active band is small and not at all when it is large, with no memorize-then-generalize delay. Active support governs the outcome, acting through the teacher-weighted Gram spectrum. The authors restrict the claim to the positive-ridge regime and to linear read-outs. They expect the delay to return as λ → 0, on a timescale set by the smallest teacher-weighted eigenvalue.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a linear read-out trained by full-batch gradient descent over a fixed, structured Fourier character map, not a jointly trained small neural network. It fixes p = 97, n = 3763, and λ = 10⁻² for the main dynamic sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with band radius and active support: at fixed nominal dimension M = 32, masking to 1089 active modes gives 1.000 held-out accuracy, while the full 4225-mode band gives 0.185. The paper uses one training-set size and one weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed nominal dimension (M = 32), the number of active Fourier modes, not the parameter count or capacity ratio, determines whether held-out accuracy is perfect (≤1089 active modes) or collapses (4225). The authors frame feature-map structure as a control variable for whether grokking occurs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a fixed-feature model shows delayed generalization depends on the feature map's structure (active support / teacher-weighted spectrum), not just over-parameterization and realizability.

record.code_released: Code and seeds are available from the authors upon request.
record.peer_reviewed: OPT2026: 18th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning
record.problems: The main sweeps use one training-set size and one weight-decay value. The detailed trajectory is a single realization at M = 24. Peak accuracy is an upper envelope over finite training runs, although the paper also gives a ridge fixed-point argument for the collapse.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (one n = 3763 only); trainable or nonlinear networks (only a linear read-out over fixed features); zero or small weight decay (only λ = 10⁻²).
No circuit formation, memorization-removal or progress measures are tracked. The null-space mass is a coordinate quantity, not a generalizing-circuit measure.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation for a lazy-to-rich transition.
One weight decay and one dataset size, so no critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs or architectures.

missing.what: A preliminary observation at λ = 0 is described as consistent with a long memorize-then-generalize separation at the band radii that collapse at λ = 10⁻². No numbers are given, and it is deferred to a full-length version. This would bear on V1 holding in this system without weight decay.
t1, t2 or training trajectories for the small-band and masked runs that the authors call gapless. Only peak held-out accuracy is reported, so the absence of delay there is asserted, not measured.
Training accuracy for the M ≥ 28 sweep points. Without it, a researcher cannot tell whether memorization occurred there.
The authors mention observing dynamical failures of a − b at small M under a nonlinear read-out, but report no numbers.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' labels are downgraded to limits_scope. The system is a linear read-out on frozen features, unlike the trained networks of the originals, and the authors expect grokking to reappear at zero ridge, so the result delimits V1 rather than refuting it. Rows reporting near-perfect peak accuracy cannot show the absence of a delay, because peak accuracy is not a timing measure. Table 1 closed-form results at λ = 10⁻⁶ are static and correctly left out. The study also contradicts the cited XVS ridge-regression grokking result, which is not one of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses one training-set size, n = 3763, and does not test how the delay varies as the training set shrinks. Its detailed training trajectory is reported only for M = 24.
It does not track formation of a generalizing circuit or memorizing components, or test whether continuous progress measures anticipate a generalization jump.
It tests neither non-algorithmic data nor initialization-scale or weight-norm changes that induce a lazy-to-rich transition.
It does not study LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
It uses one positive weight-decay setting and varies feature support, not training-set size; it does not test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
It does not compare algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax.

rows.subject: linear read-out over band-limited character feature map
rows.operation_detail: Training-trajectory measurement of train and held-out accuracy alongside null-space mass
rows.value: Training accuracy reaches 1.00; held-out accuracy reaches 0.91 by step ∼ 10,000 and then does not move. No late upswing.
rows.note: The authors report the held-out plateau while null-space mass continues to decay, and identify the absence of a late rise as evidence against a grokking delay.
rows.check: State is correct. It is a single seed: training reaches 1.00 and held-out plateaus at 0.91 by about step 10k with no late rise through 25k+ steps.

relationships.condition: Linear ridge read-out over a fixed structured Fourier feature map, target a − b, p = 97, n = 3763, λ = 10⁻², band radius M ≥ 24 (unmasked)
relationships.reason: Training fits (1.00 at M = 24), but held-out accuracy plateaus at 0.91 with no late upswing (r13). Peak held-out falls to 0.506, 0.185 and 0.066 at larger bands (r3–r6, r12). The delayed jump does not occur at positive ridge in this fixed-feature linear system.
relationships.display_finding: At M=24, training accuracy reached 1.00 while held-out accuracy plateaued at 0.91 without a late upswing; larger bands reduced peak held-out accuracy to 0.506, 0.185, and 0.066.
